people.name: Tyler Joseph
people.description: Tyler Joseph American singer, songwriter, multi-instrumentalist, record producer, and rapper and lead vocalist for the musical duo Twenty One Pilots. Their second album the 2015 Blurryface peaked at No.1 on the US chart.

people.name: Janelle Monáe
people.description: American singer, songwriter, and rapper Janelle Monáe appeared on the 2011 single 'We Are Young' alongside Fun, reaching No. 1 in multiple countries. In 2023, 'We Are Young' accumulated 1 billion streams on Spotify.

people.name: Brad Delson
people.description: Brad Delson serves as the guitarist and a founding member of the rock band Linkin Park, which achieved the 2002 US No.2 and UK No.4 single 'In The End', alongside the 2002 US No.2 and 2001 UK No.4 album Hybrid Theory. Recognized among the best-selling music acts in history, Linkin Park has achieved worldwide sales exceeding 100 million records. The group's accolades include two Grammy Awards, seven American Music Awards, four Billboard Music Awards, four MTV Video Music Awards, 10 MTV Europe Music Awards, and three World Music Awards.

people.name: Isaiah "Ikey" Owens
people.description: American keyboardist Isaiah "Ikey" Owens gained recognition for his performances with The Mars Volta, Jack White, and various groups from the Long Beach music scene. At the age of 39, Owens passed away from a heart attack on October 14, 2014, inside his hotel room in Puebla, Mexico.

people.name: Greg Upchurch
people.description: Greg Upchurch is the drummer for the American rock band 3 Doors Down. The group achieved a US No. 4 single in 2003 with "When I'm Gone" and a US No. 1 album in 2005 with "Seventeen Days".

people.name: Sam Reid
people.description: Sam Reid is a founding keyboardist for the Canadian rock band Glass Tiger, known for their 1986 UK No. 29 single 'Don't Forget Me When I'm Gone'. Alongside his band, he received five Canadian Music Industry Juno Awards, earned multiple Canadian SOCAN Classic Awards, and secured a Grammy Award nomination for Best New Artist.

people.name: Stephen Jansen
people.description: English musician Stephen Jansen belongs to the band Japan. During the late 1970s and early 1980s, the group achieved success by releasing nine UK Top 40 hits. These included the 1982 Top 5 single 'Ghosts' and the live album Oil on Canvas in 1983, which reached the UK Top 5.

people.name: Julee Cruise
people.description: Julee Cruise was an American singer, songwriter, and actress. She had a hit in 1990 with the single 'Falling', which reached No. 7 in the UK and served as the theme music for the television show Twin Peaks. Throughout the 1990s, Cruise toured as a member of the B-52's, taking the place of Cindy Wilson. Cruise passed away on 9 June 2022 at the age of 65 in Pittsfield, Massachusetts, with her passing determined to be a suicide by suffocation.

people.name: Gwen Dickey
people.description: American-born British singer Gwen Dickey gained recognition as the lead vocalist of the R&B group Rose Royce, performing under the moniker Rose Norwalt. The group achieved late-70s chart successes with the tracks 'Car Wash' and 'Wishing on a Star'.

people.name: Jaco Pastorius
people.description: American jazz bassist, composer, and producer Jaco Pastorius achieved the 1976 hit 'Birdland' with Weather Report and collaborated with Joni Mitchell, Herbie Hancock, and Pat Metheny. His playing style drew on funk and featured fretless bass, lyrical solos, bass chords, and innovative harmonic techniques. Pastorius passed away on September 21st, 1987, at the age of 35, following an altercation with a bouncer at the Midnight Club in Fort Lauderdale that left him beaten into a coma and suffering from irreversible brain damage.

people.name: Gilbert O\'Sullivan
people.description: Irish singer-songwriter Gilbert O'Sullivan achieved the 1972 UK No.1 single 'Clair' and the 1972 US No.1 single 'Alone Again Naturally', along with 13 additional UK Top 40 singles. Across the globe, he has placed 16 records in the top 40, which includes six No. 1 songs. Additionally, he has been honored with three Ivor Novello Awards, featuring Songwriter of the Year in 1973.

people.name: Oliver Brown
people.description: Oliver Brown was an American percussionist and an original member of KC & The Sunshine Band, known for performing on the late 70's hits 'That's the Way (I Like It)' and '(Shake, Shake, Shake) Shake Your Booty'.

people.name: Bette Midler
people.description: American singer, actress, comedian and author Bette Midler. She had the 1989 US No.1 & UK No.5 single 'Wind Beneath my Wings'. She won Grammy Awards for Best New Artist, Best Female Pop Vocal Performance for The Rose, based on the life of Janis Joplin and won Record of the Year for 'Wind Beneath my Wings'.

people.name: John Densmore
people.description: John Densmore served as the drummer for The Doors, a rock act of the 1960s that ranked among the most influential and controversial groups of the era, largely driven by the lyrics, voice, erratic stage persona, and legal issues of singer Jim Morrison. The band released the 1967 single 'Light My Fire', which reached No.1 in the US and No.49 in the UK, as well as the 1971 single 'Riders On The Storm'. At a later point, Densmore permitted 'Riders on the Storm' to be used in a Pirelli Tyres commercial exclusively in the UK; afterwards, he stated that he "heard Jim's voice" in his ears and chose to donate the earnings to charity. In 2002, Densmore turned down a $15 million offer from Cadillac for 'Break on Through (To the Other Side)' due to Morrison's strong opposition against licensing the music of the Doors for commercial purposes.

people.name: Eric Bloom
people.description: Eric Bloom provides guitar and vocals for the American hard rock band Blue Oyster Cult. The group achieved success with the single '(Don't Fear) The Reaper', which reached No.12 in the US in 1976 and No.16 in the UK in 1978. Worldwide, Blue Oyster Cult have sold more than 24 million records.

people.name: Charlie Grima
people.description: Charlie Grima is an English drummer associated with the band Wizzard, which released the 1973 UK No. 1 single 'See My Baby Jive' alongside the 1973 Christmas single 'I Wish It Could Be Christmas Everyday'.

people.name: Sandy Nelson
people.description: Sandy Nelson was an American drummer known for his 1962 single "Let There Be Drums", which reached No.3 in the UK and No.7 in the US. Throughout his career, he collaborated with The Teddy Bears and Gene Vincent. Following a motorcycle accident at the end of 1963, Nelson suffered injuries that required the amputation of his right foot and part of his leg. Despite this, he kept recording and playing the drums. Nelson passed away in Las Vegas on 14 February 2022, at the age of 83, due to complications from a stroke.

people.name: Lou Rawls
people.description: US singer Lou Rawls put out over 60 albums and moved more than 40 million records. His single 'You'll Never Find Another Love Like Mine' reached No.2 in the US and No.10 in the UK in 1976. Rawls passed away at age 72 from lung cancer on January 6th, 2006.

people.name: Billy Paul
people.description: Billy Paul was an American soul singer famous for his single 'Me and Mrs Jones', which reached No. 1 in the US in 1972 and No. 12 in the UK in 1973. He belonged to the group of artists connected to the Philadelphia soul sound. Paul passed away on 24th April 2016 at the age of 81 due to pancreatic cancer.

people.name: Matt Monro
people.description: English singer Matt Monro, known as "The Man with the Golden Voice", achieved the 1964 single "Walk Away", which reached No.4 in the UK and No.23 in the US. He also landed 10 additional UK Top 40 hits, featuring his 1965 success with his rendition of The Beatles's "Yesterday". On 7 February 1985, he passed away from liver cancer at the Cromwell Hospital in Ealing, London.

works.title: Midnights
works.eventDescription: American singer-songwriter Taylor Swift claimed the top spot on the US chart with Midnights, her tenth studio album. The release shattered multiple global records, setting a Spotify milestone for the highest number of single-day streams for an album while reaching No. 1 across 28 territories.

works.title: One Dance
works.eventDescription: In 2016, Drake achieved the title of Spotify's most-streamed artist, while his track 'One Dance' became the platform's top song. During the year, the Canadian accumulated 4.7 billion total streams, with his album Views accounting for over half of that total. The single 'One Dance' alone garnered 960 million streams, an amount that would require more than 5,200 years to play back-to-back.

works.title: Tales of Brave Ulysses
works.eventDescription: Australian artist, cartoonist, songwriter and film-maker Martin Sharp died from emphysema aged 71. Sharp was called Australia's foremost pop artist.His psychedelic posters of Bob Dylan, Donovan and others, rank as classics of the genre. Martin co-wrote one of Cream's best known songs, ‘Tales of Brave Ulysses’, created the cover art for Cream's Disraeli Gears and Wheels of Fire albums, and in the 1970s became a champion of singer Tiny Tim.

works.title: Last Christmas
works.eventDescription: According to the Performing Right Society, Wham's 1984 track Last Christmas ranked as the most played festive song over a five-year period. It narrowly beat Band Aid's Do They Know It's Christmas?, which placed second on the seasonal chart. In third position was The Pogues featuring the late Kirsty MacColl with Fairytale of New York, a recording originally issued in 1987. Additional artists appearing on the list included Slade, Mariah Carey, and Bruce Springsteen.

works.title: Dream Runner
works.eventDescription: American rock singer-songwriter Ray Gillen died age 34 from an AIDS related disease in a New York Hospital. works.title: Ice Ice Baby
works.eventDescription: Vanilla Ice began a four-week reign at the top of the UK singles chart with 'Ice Ice Baby'. The song utilized a sample of the bass introduction from the Queen and David Bowie chart-topper 'Under Pressure'. Initially issued as the B-side to the rapper's rendition of 'Play That Funky Music', 'Ice Ice Baby' transitioned to the A-side after American disc jockeys began airing it.

works.title: Everybody's Rockin'
works.eventDescription: Geffen Records filed a lawsuit against Neil Young on the grounds that his newly submitted material for the label was uncommercial and differed musically from his past work. His most recent release, Everybody's Rockin', consisted of original tracks and cover songs in a rockabilly style, totaling only 25 minutes in length and becoming his briefest album.

Country singer Lynn Anderson recorded a cover of the track, scoring her initial hit by climbing to No.2 on the US country singles charts during mid-1973.

works.title: Axis: Bold as Love
works.eventDescription: The Jimi Hendrix Experience put out their second studio album, Axis: Bold as Love. Hendrix voiced disappointment about the cover art, featuring himself and the Experience portrayed as different manifestations of Vishnu, which used a painting by Roger Law based on a photo-portrait by Karl Ferris. Hendrix remarked that a cover emphasizing his American Indian heritage would have suited the release better.

works.title: Sgt. Pepper’s Lonely Hearts Club Band
works.eventDescription: Jimi Hendrix, Pink Floyd, The Move, Nice, Outer Limits, and Amen Corner performed at the Central Hall in Chatham. The Chatham Standard subsequently published a review stating that Hendrix began his performance with the Beatles song Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band, noting that the three-member band produced the impact of a full studio ensemble. The review also mentioned that he performed several of his own tracks, which featured flawless renditions of 'Hey Joe' and 'Purple Haze', alongside the Troggs song 'Wild Thing'.

works.title: Green, Green Grass of Home
works.eventDescription: Tom Jones was at No.1 on the UK singles chart with his version of 'Green Green Grass Of Home.' It stayed at No.1 for seven weeks, giving Decca records its first million-selling single by a British artist. Also a No.11 hit in the US.

works.title: To Know Him Is to Love Him
works.eventDescription: The Teddy Bears secured the No. 1 position on the US singles chart with 'To Know Him is to Love Him.' This Phil Spector track was drawn from the inscription on his father's tombstone, reading 'To Know Him Was to Love Him.' The single remained at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 chart for three weeks and climbed to No. 2 on the UK's New Musical Express chart. Later, Dolly Parton, Linda Ronstadt, and Emmylou Harris revived the track, and their Trio version reached the peak of the US country singles chart in 1987.

Nelson passed away in Las Vegas on 14 February 2022, at the age of 83, due to complications from a stroke.

works.title: You'll Never Find Another Love Like Mine
works.eventDescription: US singer Lou Rawls put out over 60 albums and moved more than 40 million records. His single 'You'll Never Find Another Love Like Mine' reached No.2 in the US and No.10 in the UK in 1976. Rawls passed away at age 72 from lung cancer on January 6th, 2006.

works.title: Me and Mrs. Jones
works.eventDescription: Billy Paul was an American soul singer famous for his single 'Me and Mrs Jones', which reached No. 1 in the US in 1972 and No. 12 in the UK in 1973. He belonged to the group of artists connected to the Philadelphia soul sound. Paul passed away on 24th April 2016 at the age of 81 due to pancreatic cancer.

works.title: Walk Away
works.eventDescription: English singer Matt Monro, known as "The Man with the Golden Voice", achieved the 1964 single "Walk Away", which reached No.4 in the UK and No.23 in the US. He also landed 10 additional UK Top 40 hits, featuring his 1965 success with his rendition of The Beatles's "Yesterday". On 7 February 1985, he passed away from liver cancer at the Cromwell Hospital in Ealing, London.
